source_locator: R2225: ch. IX; R2227: Part VI, ch. 9
notes: Miller, ch. IX, and Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9: the 132nd Regimental Combat Team (less the 1st Battalion and A Battery, 247th Field Artillery) landed on 8 December 1942. Confidence 0.7. The absent 1st Battalion is not invented as a separate location.

source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The Capture of Mount Austen
current_activity: attacking into the jungle on the Mount Austen crest from Hill 35
notes: Miller, ch. X: on 18 December 1942 L Company, then the main body of 3rd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, advanced from Hill 35 onto the Mount Austen crest, met fire, and dug a perimeter just inside the jungle (one casualty). The regiment had been ordered on 16 December to occupy Mount Austen. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. Zimmerman, ch. IX, describes the 16 December relief into the west sector facing Mount Austen but does not date this first crest attack.

location_qualifier: Hill 31 and the ravine toward the Gifu
source_locator: R2225: ch. X, Attacks Against the Gifu Strong Point, 24-30 December
current_activity: reaching Hill 31 and being halted by machine-gun fire from the Gifu
notes: Miller, ch. X: on 24 December 1942 3rd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, reached Hill 31, was halted by machine-gun fire as it moved south into the jungle, and dug in in the ravine between Hills 31 and 32. 1st Battalion was in position by 1230. This opened the attacks against the Gifu strong point. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The Capture of Hill 27
current_activity: capturing Hill 27 and holding it against six Japanese counterattacks
notes: Miller, ch. X: the 132nd Infantry attacked at 0630 on 2 January 1943. 2nd Battalion, having marched to the south-east slope of Hill 27 the day before, gained the summit by 0907 and had all assault troops on top by 1130, surprising a Japanese howitzer crew. It then held the hill against six infantry counterattacks that afternoon, losing eight killed and seventy wounded, and spent the night on the reverse slope. 1st and 3rd Battalions pressed the eastern Gifu. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The Capture of Hill 27
current_activity: holding a half-moon line around the eastern bulge of the Gifu
notes: Miller, ch. X: by 1000 on 4 January 1943 patrols of the 1st and 2nd Battalions had established contact, and the 132nd Infantry was holding a half-moon line around the eastern bulge of the Gifu between Hills 31 and 27. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XII, Reduction of the Gifu
current_activity: being relieved at the Gifu and returning to the Lunga perimeter
notes: Miller, ch. XII: on 9 January 1943 the 2nd Battalion, 35th Infantry, and the 25th Division Cavalry Reconnaissance Troop completed the relief of the 132nd Infantry, which returned to the Lunga perimeter. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, The South Coast
current_activity: landing the reinforced 2nd Battalion unopposed at Verahue
notes: Miller, ch. XV: the reinforced 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, left Kukum on the evening of 31 January 1943, arrived off Nugu Point at dawn on 1 February, and, after the beachmaster agreed Verahue was clear, began unloading there under fighter cover. By 1500 all troops and supplies were ashore. The claim locates the regiment by that 2nd Battalion landing, which is the body Miller names. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. Zimmerman, ch. IX, confirms the south-coast expedition but does not give this landing day.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal
current_activity: advancing from Marovovo to Kamimbo Bay after finding abandoned landing craft
notes: Miller, ch. XV: on the morning of 8 February 1943 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, left Marovovo, found abandoned Japanese landing craft and supplies on the beach, realised the enemy was evacuating, narrowed its front, and advanced to Kamimbo Bay. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal; R2226: ch. IX, The Final Drive
current_activity: meeting 1st Battalion, 161st Infantry, at Tenaro, ending organised fighting
notes: Miller, ch. XV, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that on 9 February 1943 the American south-coast and north-coast forces met near Cape Esperance, ending organised fighting on Guadalcanal. Miller dates the meeting at Tenaro between 1600 and 1700, when 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry, marched into the village and met 1st Battalion, 161st Infantry. Zimmerman describes the pincer ending that day (he writes Tanamba River for the Tenamba/Tenaemba). Confidence 0.7.
